argument:
The bear correctly rejects headline P/E as clean recurring value when fair-value and remeasurement gains contribute 51.31% of PBT. The narrower counterweight is that CFO rose to RM2.391bn from RM1.060bn and retained RM1.780bn after the specified property, equipment and land spending. Operating cash improvement therefore exists independently of treating noncash gains as owner earnings.

Acquisition and deposit spending still required net borrowing, and RM21.818bn net debt leaves a substantial financing burden. The higher-risk purchase scenario is completed acquisitions and property operations improving recurring cash enough to reduce that dependence; no verified recurring valuation proves this is priced in. Actual cash-generating operations keep that scenario plausible, while forward P/E of 17.71x is more relevant than 8.54x headline earnings. Buying remains speculative until asset conversion and funding discipline substantiate shareholder participation.
key_points: Noncash gains invalidate a simple headline-P/E bargain.
Operating cash improved after specified ordinary asset spending.
Acquisition returns must reduce observed borrowing dependence.
rebuttal_to_previous: Funding dependence is real. However, RM1.780bn remains from operating CFO after the specified ordinary asset spending before acquisitions and interest; the operating engine is not solely noncash profit. This supports a speculative conversion thesis without declaring debt manageable or valuation already cheap.
